findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/prose-size.ts::validate-adapters byte-ratchet lines name the baseline relative to the skills dir, not as an absolute path
findings.title: validate-adapters byte-ratchet lines name the baseline relative to the skills dir, not as an absolute path
findings.action: No change: the relative path is still the spec's <path>, and the absolute form tripped a sibling test's output match.
findings.disposition_rationale: Spec §3 gives the INFO line as 'no baseline at <path>'; a skills-dir-relative path satisfies it and keeps temp-dir names out of output that other tests pattern-match.

occurrences.title: validate-adapters byte-ratchet lines name the baseline relative to the skills dir, not as an absolute path

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/prose-size.ts::fail-closed baseline guarantee is keyed to flag absence, not to the bundled tree
findings.title: fail-closed baseline guarantee is keyed to flag absence, not to the bundled tree
findings.refutation: Spec §4.2 'Absent baseline fails closed on the bundled tree only' chooses exactly this: CI runs validate-adapters with no flags, so deleting the file cannot disable the gate; an explicit --skills-dir (fixtures, an adopter's dir) skips with INFO. docs/guide/cli.md states both halves.
findings.disposition_rationale: The behaviour is the spec's chosen design and is documented; a present-but-broken baseline fails in both cases.

occurrences.title: fail-closed baseline guarantee is keyed to flag absence, not to the bundled tree

findings.title: parseLsTree silently drops covered files whose paths git C-quotes
findings.action: tally reads git ls-tree -r -l -z and parseLsTree splits on NUL; a test covers a path with a space and a non-ASCII name.
findings.disposition_rationale: Fixed in e7732934 with a regression test.

occurrences.title: parseLsTree silently drops covered files whose paths git C-quotes

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/prose-size.ts::coveredfiles/measure throw on an unreadable skills dir, escaping as an uncaught exception
findings.title: coveredFiles/measure throw on an unreadable skills dir, escaping as an uncaught exception
findings.action: proseRatchet and baseline --lower catch a measure failure: a FAIL prose-baseline.json line and exit 2 respectively.
findings.disposition_rationale: Fixed in e7732934 with an in-process test. validate-adapters' pre-existing per-skill loop still throws earlier on an unreadable skill subdirectory; that predates this change and is out of scope.

occurrences.title: coveredFiles/measure throw on an unreadable skills dir, escaping as an uncaught exception

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/prose-size.ts::--scope hot silently degrades when a hot file is renamed or removed
findings.title: --scope hot silently degrades when a hot file is renamed or removed
findings.disposition_rationale: hot is a named convenience scope fixed by the spec to the three orchestrator files; a rename or removal still appears as a negative delta row on the commit that made it, so it is visible in the tally rather than silent.

occurrences.title: --scope hot silently degrades when a hot file is renamed or removed

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/prose-size.ts::measure/coveredfiles follow symlinks, so a symlinked covered file can dodge or spuriously trip the ratchet
findings.title: measure/coveredFiles follow symlinks, so a symlinked covered file can dodge or spuriously trip the ratchet
findings.disposition_rationale: No covered file is a symlink in the repo; installs symlink whole skill directories, which statSync must follow. A file-level symlink would show as a ratchet-vs-tally mismatch, not a silent pass of real growth in the committed tree.

occurrences.title: measure/coveredFiles follow symlinks, so a symlinked covered file can dodge or spuriously trip the ratchet
